column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Article's Rilindja section says roots in late 18th century; entry says nothing contradictory. Article places the Illyrian Wars/Roman integration only in the lead; no dates given, so left general.
Article lead says authoritarian republic emerged in 1830s; omitted as an assessment-like label. Entry says Mapuche resistance ended 1880s; article says 'late 19th century' — wording kept general.

Left out: the article's lead statements on apartheid and genocide (contested present-day characterisations), the Second Intifada and the 2020s. Article says Arabic downgraded to special status in 2018; omitted.

Article says Christian Bible is translated or being translated into about half the world's languages; sales figure already in entry. Left out Bible museums and illustrations detail beyond Book of Kells.

Entry says Portuguese republic 1910, dictatorship 1926, democracy 1976; consistent. Article gives 1975 coup in 'Return to democracy' (likely meaning 25 November 1975); omitted. Article's lead says remained 'trends towards autocratisation'; omitted as assessment.

Article gives the Nov-stated 2026 earthquake and 21st-century security improvements; omitted (assessments, recent). Article says Gran Colombia period began 1819 (in desc). Article mentions 1810 'United Provinces of New Granada' (in desc).

Article's 'Iceland as a possession' lead says Treaty of Kiel 1814 'formally retained'; in entry as 'ceded'; left out. Article: Althing 'founded 930' in Government section; tradition. Omitted modern politics and rankings.

The entry's stub description mentions Nader Shah and Erekle II; the article text given has nothing on them. Left out the post-2024 political crisis and disputed offices. Article says Georgian scripts 'invented by King Pharnavaz I' per tradition; omitted.

Entry says autonomous republic of RSFSR then union republic 1936; consistent. Left out the article's assessments of government, rankings and political reforms. Article says Botai 'BC' - converted to BCE.
Article dates the Maurya Empire 'c. 320–185 BC' (converted to BCE). Left out 2024 events, human-rights and corruption material. 'Pakistani forces carried out genocide' stated in entry; not repeated.
Article quotes Collins's phrase loosely; paraphrased from the 'not the ultimate freedom ... but the freedom to achieve it' quote. Left out rankings, economy, society sections.
Left out the 2014 protests and the Dayton viceroy comparison. Article's Austro-Hungarian note about Sanjak of Novi Pazar omitted.

Article gives Nandi leadership of Koitalel as 1890–1906 in one section and 1890–1900 in another; end date left out. Entry says protectorate 1895 and the article says British East Africa Protectorate from 1889; neither printed. Left out Kenyatta-era corruption claims, human rights, and all post-2013 elections as disputed or recent assessments.
Article calls the 1944 re-occupation and 45-year Latvian SSR period; in entry. Left out rankings, politics 2010-2016, health.
Article says Luxembourg regained independence in 1867 (entry: after Luxembourg Crisis); consistent. Left out tax-haven, rankings, human rights.

Article gives King Bodin's death as 1101 or 1108; hedge kept. Left out 1991-95 role in the attack on Dubrovnik, EU accession status, politics and rankings. Entry says semi-autonomy 1696; article gives the autonomy in the 16th century and Ottoman rule 1496-1878, so the 1696 date is not repeated.

Entry says the Genoese built a castle in the early 1200s; article says refounded as a Genoese colony in 1215, castle not mentioned, so castle omitted. Article's 1963 customs agreement and CIA Factbook note about 1419 independence omitted. Left out wealth, tax and money-laundering material.

Article's lead says 'Kyrgyzstan was first established as the Yenisei Kyrgyz Khaganate'; the 840 CE date is from the Early history section. Left out the Dzungar and Qing material, rankings, human rights.

Article gives Independence Day celebrated as 24 May 1822 and also 9 October 1820 for Guayaquil; only the latter printed. Article has Roldós death 'many people believe assassinated by CIA'; left out as unsupported claim. Article's lead notes a 2026 hunger report; omitted.

Article gives population as 41,389 (lead) and 40,542 (August 2026): disagree, so no figure printed. Entry says fully independent in 1866; article says formed 1719 and independent on dissolution of German Confederation 1866; consistent.

The article gives both 1683 (defeat of Koxinga's grandson, 'annexed in 1683' in the lead) and May 1684 (formal annexation); the entry says 1683 for the Qing takeover. Left the Qing annexation date out entirely, and the Dutch period, which the article hardly covers. Population: the article gives 23.9 million in the lead and 23.3 million under Demographics; wrote 'more than 23 million'. The article's own phrase for the Treaty of Shimonoseki cession is 1895; consistent with the entry.

The article dates the Nabataean kingdom to the third century BC in the lead and to 169 BC in the Classical section; the dates are left out. The entry only says 'later'. Entry says Emirate established 1921 and independence 1946; article agrees. The article says the Arab Revolt 'ended four centuries of stagnation' (judgement; left out). Population figures in the article vary (11.5 million lead, 9.5 million 2015 census); left out.

Population: article has 34,042 (2025), 33,559 (2026) and 33,896 (2023); omitted. Entry says borders unchanged since 1463; the article does not mention it, so not repeated. The Statutes of 1600 'earliest written governing documents still in effect' is given as 'considered to be' in the article; I wrote only that they remain at the core.

The article gives 1894 for the French takeover in the lead and 1892 in the Colonial section; the entry says 1894. Left the year out. The lead says French Dahomey was part of French West Africa from the takeover; the body says 1899; used 1899 only as the year the article gives for inclusion. Entry says 'Marxist–Leninist coup led to renaming in 1975'; the article calls the coup the 1972 Dahomeyan coup d'état and the renaming 30 November 1975. I wrote 'after a Marxist–Leninist military coup' without a year. Omitted the article's judgement about former president Talon, population figures (11.5 million vs 15 million), and rankings.

The entry's civil war death estimate (above 100,000) is not in the article; not repeated. The entry says Soviet republic on 5 December 1929; article agrees. Left out: the article's characterisations of the present government and human rights record, GDP and remittance figures, population figures (10.4 million in 2023, over 11 million in the lead). The article lists many dynasties in its lead but gives details only for the Samanids; the Samanid Empire's dates 819–999 are from the article.

Article says the Duar War was in the 19th century, and gives no year for the Wangchuck dynasty's emergence; entry does not give years either. Population differs between article passages (800,871 lead, 777,486 in 2021); wrote 'about 800,000'. Left out: rankings (Freedom House, Global Peace Index, SAARC ranks), the bitcoin holdings, named prime ministers, bare 'Last Shangri-La' phrase.

Entry says the territory became the Sheikdom of Kuwait in 1752 and a British protectorate in 1899; the article only gives 1752 and 1899 in its lead, and the History section 'Pre-oil' gives no 1752 detail; consistent, but I left the years out. Left out: the article's section on citizenship revocations since 2024 and a '2026 Iran war' heading (no text), because it is written as a political assessment; also the article's classification of Kuwait as an autocracy, the genocide accusation against the government, rankings and population figures (4.82 million). Article says Bedoon number 300,000 (1995) etc.; omitted numbers.

Entry says German East Africa in 1885; the article says 1885 in the lead but 1891 for the German Empire's takeover of the company's rights in the body. Left the year out. The article gives 250,000 deaths 1962–1993 and 300,000 in the civil war; used as the article gives them. Population figures differ (over 14 million lead, 12.3 million 2021); omitted. Left out the article's judgements on the CNDD–FDD, human-rights and poverty rankings.

The entry says the Torrijos–Carter Treaties provided for transfer on 31 December 1999; the article agrees and adds the surrounding territory was returned in 1979. Not repeated. Left out: rankings, GDP figures, tax-haven section and population estimates beyond 'over 4 million'. The article says the Spanish American Wars of independence; 'Grito' act met with disdain in Veraguas and the capital; kept brief.

The article has the army abolished on 1 December 1948 and permanently by the constitution of 1949; entry says the constitution of 1949 abolished it permanently; consistent. The article describes independence in 1821 as part of the First Mexican Empire (lead), which differs from its History section (Guatemala declared independence of all Central America); I told the 15 September 1821 account only. Left out the current president, indices, rankings, GDP and tourism figures.

The article's lead says 'Hausa is the official and national language'; I left official language out as unclear/likely wrong (French is not mentioned in the file). The article's 'Mali Empire' subsection is empty, so nothing on the pre-colonial states beyond the lead's mention; the colonial section only lists explorers. Entry says distinct colony in 1922, French Community 1958; not repeated. The article says the Diori regime used a 'positive' relationship with other states except Dahomey; omitted. Left out poverty-index and insurgency judgements.

The article gives no founding date for Copán or the Maya decline mentioned in the entry; not repeated. The 2024 population ('exceeding 10 million') omitted. Left out: the poverty statistics, the 2013/2017 election fraud claims and the 2025 election because the article presents them in contested terms I could not attribute fully; also the article's 'Spanish conquest (1524–1539)' heading has only the Columbus text. Article says 'banana republic' was 'originally coined to describe Honduras'; entry says the same.

The entry says Armed conflict in the early 1990s ended in a power-sharing agreement in 2000; the article agrees. The entry has the colony established by treaties with Dir-Somali and Afar sultans; the article's History section dates specific treaties of 1862 and 1885, which I used. Article says Khufu (4th Dynasty) had Punt gold; I used only Sahure as it states. Left out: Freedom House rating, Economist Democracy Index, the named president and prime minister, military spending.

Article's text on present-day rulers is a political assessment (repressive, totalitarian), human-rights and corruption sections; left out. The statement that Niyazov led until 2006 is neutral. The article gives no date for the Achaemenid annexation; the 8th and 10th centuries are as stated. The Wikipedia history section on Turkmenistan is very short; the Seljuk, Russian and Soviet matters come from the lead and politics section.

Article says the sultanate under Bolkiah (1485–1528) is 'claimed' to have controlled most of Borneo; the entry has the same; not repeated. Article's oil section is slightly inconsistent: 'Petroleum was discovered in 1929' and well drilled 1928 struck oil 5 April 1929; consistent. It also gives the British Malayan Petroleum Company formed 22 July 1922 (omitted). Left out the 2013 announcement about sharia penal code (attributed material available but kept the text neutral), HDI/GDP rankings, 'technically under martial law' comment.

Entry and article agree on 1960 independence and the 2023 coup. The entry says Bantu settlement began in the 13th century BCE; the article gives the same. Left out: HDI and GDP rankings, Françafrique characterisation beyond the entry, and constitutional details (term limits). Article says 'Some Bantu groups lived in the area when France officially occupied it in 1885'; used as 'France officially occupied it in 1885'.

The entry says Portugal withdrew in 1975 and independence came in 2002; the article gives a 'Portuguese era (1769–1975)' heading and 'Portuguese influence in the sixteenth century'; consistent. The article calls the Indonesian occupation 'the East Timor genocide'; I did not use that label. Population 1.44 million (2026 census) not used. Left out: statements about political dominance of the executive in practice.

Entry says the Portuguese garrison arrived in 1558 and that republic status followed a referendum in 1968; the article does not mention the referendum, only a presidential republic in 1968. Dhovemi's conversion date is 1153 (or 1193), as in the entry; I kept the article's hedge. Population (515,132 in 2022) omitted; left out Human Rights section, Freedom House, current president and the 2024 election.

The entry says British protectorate on 3 November 1916; the article gives 1916 only. Entry says Mohammed bin Thani's agreement 1868; article agrees. Left out: assessments of the emir's rule, the Shura Council elections, human rights, censorship, the current emir, rankings and population totals. The article's earlier 'Murwab' text says Abbasid; I wrote 9th century as it dates the remains.

The article's lead says the region was incorporated into the Viceroyalty of New Spain, and the colonial section says the Captaincy General (1609) was a division of New Spain; used the latter. Entry says 1524 conquest; the article lead says 1524 too, while the 'European arrival (1522)' section covers Niño's visit. Entry says the federation dissolved in 1841; article agrees. The article's statement about the 1821 'joined Federal Republic' vs 1823 differ internally (1821 vs lead 1823); I left the federation entry date out. Left out the 'Bukele era', incarceration, gang crackdown and 'human rights' material as present-day assessments; also the 'lowest inequality' indicator.

Article gives Pomeroon 1581; entry does not mention it, no conflict. Left out the article's oil-economy rankings and growth figures, poverty figures and the LGBT-rights paragraph as present-day assessments/indices. Article says 'Guyana is the only country in mainland South America with English official' - omitted as a ranking-like claim.

Article gives oil discovery 1995 (lead, history) and 1996 (economy): worded 'mid-1990s'. Article gives Fang as over 85% (lead) and 80% (demographics): left the figure out. Left out Obiang assessments, rankings, HDI, Freedom House.

Entry says the Somoza rule began 1936; the article's heading says 1936 but its text says Somoza García became president 1 January 1937: no start year printed (article text: 1 January 1937). Article gives area as 130,370 and 130,967 km2: left out. Left out assessments of the Ortega government, corruption index, GDP rankings, press freedom.
Article says Maya flourished until about 1200 (lead) and until around 900 AD (history): left out. Article also says Maya spread 1500 BC–300 AD (lead): entry has the same.

Entry says Basutoland emerged 1822; the article's lead says 'formed in 1824' and its history says 1822: no year printed for the formation. Protectorate 1868 and Crown colony 1884 agree with the entry. Left out health, HIV, rape-rate, gender and Human Development statistics.

Article gives the first English settlers as 1648 (history) and 1649 (lead); entry says 1649: no year printed for the settlement. Article says 700 islands and 2,500 cays (lead) vs 2,400 cays (geography): left vague. Left out GDP ranks, tax-haven estimates and Panama Papers.
Left out economics ('Christmas creep'), attendance figures, sport and cuisine, and the 19th-century literary revival.

Article contradicts itself about Kalinago: lead says inhabited since the 13th century (the entry repeats this), pre-colonial section says no evidence of permanent settlement: left out. Left out debt default, GDP ranks, poverty and party lists.

Article gives arrival as 21 December 1470 but notes it is sometimes given as 1471 for São Tomé and 17 January 1472 for Príncipe: no year of arrival printed. Entry says 1470. Article does not name the capital: omitted. Left out economics statistics, HDI and education-rights percentages.

Article gives population as 71,293 and 69,325 for the 2011 census: left out. Kalinago and Arawak: told with the article's own hedge. Entry says Britain took possession in 1763; the article's British-colony section says a small colony was established in 1805: not printed. Left out citizenship-by-investment, LGBT-rights, GDP and tourism-ranking material.
Left out Human Development ranking, press-freedom and human-rights assessments, Bird-family corruption allegations.

Article says first settled circa 1000 BCE (lead) and at least 3,000 years ago (history): left out. Entry says at least 3,000 years ago. Left out health statistics, rankings, poverty indices and the president's name.

Article gives German rule as 1899 (lead) and 1900–1914; NZ mandate 1920 (lead) vs 1919: no years printed for these. Entry says Tripartite Convention 1899. Left out human-rights, GDP, tourism and health figures, and the present head of state's name.

Article: first inhabited roughly 2,500 years ago (lead) vs between 1500 and 1000 BC and 888 BCE (history); entry says roughly 2,500 years ago. Only the history section's dates printed. Left out population figures (106,017 and 103,291 conflict), corruption rankings, obesity statistics, foreign relations with China.
Left out the Wahnzettel quotation and the claims about emperors. The horse tale hedged as the article hedges it.
Article dates are month-first; converted to day-first. Article gives the Kinetograph patent as 1897 but tests in 1891; only 1891 printed.
Left out freedom rating, debt figures, LGBT-rights paragraph and sports.

Entry says separate colony 1 January 1976; the article says the old colony ceased to exist 1 October 1975: same as the article. Left out disputed sea-level and land-area findings, population figure for 2026, GDP, tourism numbers, health statistics.
Left out GDP, party-political and law-enforcement detail, sports.
Left out the lists of honours and commemorations.

Article says protectorate declared June 1893 in the lead (Captain Gibson, HMS Curacoa) and March 1893 in the colonial section; entry says June 1893. Month left out. Article says 'over 1,000 smaller islands' (lead) and '992 smaller islands' (geography): count left out. Prehistory date c. 30,000-28,000 BC in the article, 30,000-28,800 BCE in the entry: wrote 'around 30,000 BCE'.
No disagreement with the entry found.
The Seagull 'written in 1895' in one place, begun 1894 in another: avoided. Entry says reception of The Seagull in 1896: not repeated.

Article says associated state with full internal self-government in 1964; entry says 1967. Year left out. Entry also says federated with Anguilla in 1882 (not in article) and West Indies Federation 1958-1962: not used. Population: roughly 48,000 (lead), around 53,000 (2019 est.), 47,606 (2021): used the 2021 count. Hamilton's birth year 1755 or 1757: left out.

Columbus's sighting is dated 22 January 1496 in the Etymology section and 1498 in History: left out. Population 109,296 (lead, undated) and 104,332 (2021): used the dated one. Inhabited islands 7 (lead) vs 9 (geography): left out. Left out the 2025 election and current office holders.
No contradiction with the entry found.

Entry says France claimed the island in 1650 and internal self-government 1967: neither is in the article, left out. Population over 184,100 (mid 2023, lead) vs 172,948 (2022 census): used the census.
No disagreement with the entry found.
No disagreement with the entry found.
No disagreement with the entry found.
Entry says 6th-4th century BCE traditional; article gives Chu 6th-century BC birth and a third account in the 4th century BCE: no century given for the man. 'Legacy' used since no death is told.

Entry says the Council of Nicaea set the date as the first Sunday after the first full moon on or after the vernal equinox; the article says later scholarship has refuted that tradition (the equinox rule only implicitly endorsed). The text now describes the rule only and says neither who set it nor when.

Population: lead says around 245,000; demographics gives the 2011 census 240,705: used the census. The expulsion is called ethnic cleansing in the article's own voice; attributed in the text. No contradiction with the entry found.
Article says shrapnel (lead) vs mortar fire (body): wrote mortar fire. No contradiction with the entry found.
Article gives 'nearly 3,500 dioceses and eparchies' (lead) and 3,171 dioceses (2021), and conflicting membership figures: all left out. Present-day controversies and the current pope left out.
No contradiction with the entry found. Credit for the assembly line: article says contemporary sources credit employees; omitted.
No contradiction with the entry found.
Entry gives c. 701-762; article agrees. Article spells the relative Li Yangbin and Li Yangbing: used the latter.
Told 'according to Genesis'. No contradiction with the entry found.

Article says fourteen books traditionally attributed (lead) vs 13 (Writings): count left out. Entry says death after 64 or a few years later; article says before 68. Conversion 31-36 (article) vs 32 CE mention: used 31 to 36.
No disagreement with the entry found.
Article says novel begun 1909 in one place and 1908 in the lead (entry 1908); I wrote only 'by 1910 he was at work'.
No disagreement with the entry.
Article's chronology of Torquay and Rottingdean is muddled; I stated both without dates beyond 1897. Left out the Dyer controversy.

Article gives two spans for the Black Paintings (1819-1822 heading, 1819-1823 lead = entry); I wrote no dates for them. Article says First Court Painter 1790 under Charles IV while the entry says Primer Pintor 1799; court ranks left out.
No disagreement with entry. Left out Baconian Shakespeare theory and contested sexuality material.
Omitted Stalin/Mussolini remarks, already in the entry.
Entry says he studied under Helmholtz and Kirchhoff and succeeded Kirchhoff in 1889; the article gives neither, so I left them out.
Left out contemporary politics, Saudi funding and the Babri mosque.

Entry says several historians hold he was poisoned; the article says only 'speculation' and the 1938 charge. Per the coordinator, the text now gives neither version of how he died (the article says officially pneumonia, speculation persists, 1938 Bukharin trial charge that Yagoda's NKVD killed him). Entry says return in 1928; article says he lived in USSR from 1932; dates avoided.

Entry says the Turkish Federated State of Cyprus was declared in 1975; the article does not mention it, so omitted. Article says Turkey took 'northern four-elevenths (about 36%)' in 1974 but the lead and geography say about a third; I used 'the north'. Left out current officeholders, Freedom House scores, economy figures and the claim 'puppet state' (contested in the article).
Article's dream story is told as his claim.
Omitted counts of sites, countries and ratifications as they are given 'as of' dates in the article.
Entry dates the civilisation from c. 1200 BCE; article says Mycenaean decline c. 1100 BC; I gave no start date.
Entry gives Fallingwater (1935) from the lead; the article's section says completed 1937; I left its date out.
No disagreement with entry.
Converted the article's BC dates to BCE.
Left out all geography counts and rankings.
Article gives no account of his marriage or death; entry's Hańska marriage and death are not in the file so left out.
Article's text on later life is thin (no Frankfurt or death details); entry says he settled in Frankfurt in 1833; not repeated. Omitted details of his private life.
Article dates the end of Egyptian prehistory to "around 3100 BC"; used as 3100 BCE. No disagreement with the entry found.

Article gives no details of the drowning (only that depression worsened after the Blitz and the reception of the Roger Fry biography); not repeated. Article says she began publishing professionally in 1904; not used.

Article says the 2002 ceremony re-interred his "ashes" but also that the body was exhumed and put in a new coffin; I wrote "remains". The desc says he was buried at his birthplace; the article says he was moved to the Panthéon in 2002 (the entry does not mention this).

Article dates the first induced nuclear reaction to 1917 in its lead but describes the nitrogen experiments as 1919 in the body (entry says 1917); I gave no year for the reaction. Article calls Rutherford and Soddy's gas thoron; omitted.

Article gives 2,996 deaths including the 19 hijackers (the entry's 2,977 excludes them); I wrote only the 2,996 total with its breakdown. Article lead says bin Laden was killed in May 2011; legal section gives 2 May 2011. Left out: rankings (deadliest attack, aviation disasters), approval ratings, the Costs of War estimate, and claims about Saudi government role.

Article gives Wells's eugenics views (largely recanted by 1940); the entry covers them, so not repeated. Article says his 1914 Russian visit was recorded in a newspaper article dated 1941: evidently a slip, omitted. Article says "dozens of short stories", more than forty novels (as the entry).

Article says she wrote 14 books in the lead and "a total of 12 published books" under Works; no number given. Article gives the National Women's Hall of Fame induction as both 1965 and 1973; left out. Article says Polly Thomson was hired when Sullivan's health began failing around 1914; I wrote "in about 1914".

Article says Paleolithic extends from "2.5 or 2.6 million years ago" while also dating Lomekwi tools to 3.3 million years; I gave no start for the Palaeolithic. Article gives Chauvet as about 36,000 BC while the Prehistory article gives a different date; omitted. Article states the Stone Age ended "between 4000 BC and 2000 BC" and elsewhere "between 6000 and 2500 BC" for much of humanity; I used only the latter, with its scope.
Article gives the Russian period as 1913-1920 (entry mentions only neoclassical 1920-1951 and serial 1954-1968, which agree).

Left out on purpose: human rights and freedom ratings, the current president, military strength figures (dated 2007), GDP and other economic figures. Article names the Soviet-era ASSR territory sizes (4,100 and 4,200 km2); not used.
Article calls him "nominated for the first and second Nobel Prizes"; not used. The article's 1953 murder claim is given as reported and attributed.
Article contradicts nothing in the entry. Left out Death in Venice biographical material about his personal life.

Article gives his birthplace as either Königsberg or Wehlau; entry says in or near Königsberg (consistent). Article does not give a day for his death date in prose other than the lead (14 February 1943); used.

Left out on purpose: the 1989 allegations about his conduct with minors and the 2026 paper disputing them (the entry mentions the allegations in one sentence; the contested biographical material would need fuller treatment than this text allows). The article names the Taoiseach in 1939; used.

Article gives the date of Cadenus and Vanessa as 1726 in the lead and 1713 in the works list; I left it out. Article gives no account of his death or burial beyond the lead dates, so I used the heading "Legacy". Tory/Whig and deanship material is already in the entry.

Article states Prufrock was written "when he was only twenty-two"; no conflict with entry. Left out: the article's statements that Eliot is "considered one of the greatest poets" and the list of honours.

Article dates Old Babylonian astrology to c. 1800 BCE; the entry gives Mesopotamia 19th-17th century BCE (consistent in range). Article says Hindu natal astrology originated with Hellenistic astrology by the 3rd century BCE; not repeated. Left out: MI5 and White House astrologers, which are about individuals in power.
Article contradicts nothing in the entry. Article gives a cause of death dispute (Waterfield attributes it to alcohol); not used.

Article gives his birthplace in the commemoration section as Düsseldorf, in the biography as Lennep; the entry says Lennep, and I did not use Düsseldorf. Article puts his wife's age at death as 80 and says she was six years older: not used.

Article says the earliest yoga practices "may have appeared in the Jain tradition at ca. 900 BCE" while the lead says "first attested in the early first millennium BCE" (consistent). Hatha Yoga Pradipika is 15th century in the article; Shiva Samhita dating (1500 or late 17th) left out.

No conflicts with the entry. Left out: the Eiffel Tower protest, the long quoted memoir about his decline, adaptations. The article says Flaubert's praise followed Boule de Suif; the entry gives 1880 for it, matching.

No conflict with the entry. Deliberately left out: the debated questions about his photographs of children and the Liddell rift (biographers disagree and the article reports speculation); migraine/Alice in Wonderland syndrome (article says no evidence he had it). Dodgson, not Carroll, used as surname in biography since the article does.

No conflict with the entry. The article says he burned 'some of his manuscripts, which contained most of the second part'; I wrote 'manuscripts' only. Left out: adaptations, monuments, national identity debate beyond one sentence.
No conflict with entry. Article dates are US month-first; converted. Death itself is not in the given excerpt, so heading is Legacy. Left out: Philosophers Camp, namesakes, musical settings.

No conflict with entry. Article: Comus first published 1634 in one place and 'anonymous edition of Comus was published in 1637' in another; I used 1637 only, but the article contradicts itself (1634 vs 1637). Entry says Paradise Lost 1667, matches. De Doctrina Christiana left out as authorship disputed.

No conflict with entry's dates (article c. 1 BC – AD 64/68, same). Article excerpt cut off at 'Non-Christian views'. Left out: Donald Fay Robinson's suggestion about Acts 12, LDS and other denominational views, apocrypha.
No conflict with entry. Article says she lived at Mårbacka 'for the rest of her life' (as entry). Left out: private relationships section beyond the friendship with Elkan, works lists.

Entry says arrived at Scutari November 1854; article gives 21 October 1854 as the date they were sent. Not contradictory, I wrote 'were sent'. Left out: Mary Seacole controversy (excerpt cut off), her views on women, theatre/film.
No conflict with entry. Article gives a lifelong affair with Viardot; I kept to 'love'. Left out: personal relationships with serfs, the steamboat fire rumours, brain weight, plays and works lists.
No conflict with entry. The article gives Feb 1548 – 17 Feb 1600; the execution date is not in the excerpt beyond '1600'. Left out: Frances Yates on Hermeticism, appearance, fiction and music.
No conflict with entry. Left out: Gallup/Siena rankings (rule), Arthur Blake etc. Article calls her widowed 1945; entry same. 'Aplastic anemia' spelled anaemia (British).
No conflict with entry. Left out: personal life (Arendt affair, Blochmann), Hermann's parentage, detailed philosophy summaries.
Article gives his birthplace as Huntington in the lead and West Hills in the body; entry says West Hills. Birthplace left out. Left out: Shakespeare authorship, religion, adaptations.
No conflict with entry dates 72-80. Seating figures left out (87,000 in Codex-Calendar vs modern ~50,000; entry already says 50,000-80,000).

No conflict with entry. The article says her father died 16 June 1874 and she did not attend the memorial; left out. Entry says she rarely left Homestead from about 1867: not in the excerpt, not repeated. Left out: relationship with Susan beyond one clause.

No conflict with entry. Article gives 'David Henry' birth name, entry lists 'David Henry Thoreau' as alias - consistent. Left out: pronunciation, autism speculation, Indian texts, sexuality, the Walden years themselves (excerpt only quotes Walden).

No conflict with entry (c. 1058–1111). Entry says he returned to teach at Nishapur in 1106: not in excerpt, not repeated. Article gives 'over 10 years' of seclusion in the lead; entry 'some ten years'; I wrote 'the decade that followed'. Excerpt cut off in the middle of the Nizam al-Mulk passage (Nizamiyya appointment date not in the excerpt).

Article says 'né Chaney' (John Griffith London né Chaney); I wrote 'born John Griffith Chaney' - the article only says né Chaney, so revise if flagged. Entry says died of uremia and late-stage alcoholism; matches. London's paternity is uncertain per article; hedged.

No conflict with entry. Article says he 'bought out his brother-in-law' in 1839 for the Mississippi plantation; I used 1835 purchase from article ('Four years later [after 1831]' sold Somerville and bought 920 acres near Coffeeville, with brother-in-law). Omitted ranking polls (rule). Mexican-American War events not in excerpt beyond lead.

No conflict with entry (dies 1821 age 25). Article says 'Keats and family marked birthday 29 Oct, baptism 31 Oct' - I used 31 October as article's headline date. Entry says Blackwood's attacked Endymion; article excerpt cites the Quarterly Review: wrote Quarterly per article and did not mention Blackwood's. Possible slip in entry vs article; left both unprinted? I printed Quarterly Review as Hunt's claim.
